literature_notes: All four ledger clips (L1–L4) describe CD80 fused C-terminally to mCherry or GFP using the '[protein]–[FP]' naming convention. CD80 is a Type I single-pass transmembrane protein: its N-terminus is extracellular (mature chain begins at residue 35 after SP cleavage at 34) and its C-terminus is intracellular (residues 269–288). A C-terminal FP fusion therefore lands in the intracellular compartment, not on the extracellular face. None of the clips names a residue, loop, or junction; none states the tag is extracellular or N-terminal. The topology_derived rule requires exactly one extracellular terminus to resolve an unspecified position — CD80 has two termini (one extracellular, one intracellular), so the rule cannot force an extracellular assignment. The notation unambiguously implies the intracellular C-terminus. No ledger line supports an extracellular surface tag site; zero sites is the correct answer.

literature_other_positions.note: CD80–mCherry C-terminal fusion expressed at the plasma membrane and functionally engaged by CTLA-4; the FP is appended after the last residue (V288) in the intracellular tail, not on the extracellular face.
